intended_object: The pure tensor b ⊗ m in the sections over U of the scalar extension of a presheaf of A-modules M along θ : A → B, i.e. in B(U) ⊗_{A(U)} M(U), where B(U) is an A(U)-module through θ_U. Inferred from the docstring, the name, and its use in `rightSectionIso_pure`, where it is the image of m ⊗ b under the symmetry isomorphism.
explanation:
`tensorSection A B theta M U` is defined as `(ModuleCat.extendScalars θ_U).obj (M.obj U)`. In Mathlib that object is the tensor product B(U) ⊗_{A(U)} M(U), where B(U) is an A(U)-module through θ_U. `leftPure` returns `TensorProduct.tmul (A.obj U) b m`, with the A(U)-module structure on B(U) taken from `rightFactor`, the restriction of scalars of B(U) along θ_U. That is the same structure that `extendScalars` uses, and the companion lemma `rightSectionIso_pure` (proved with `TensorProduct.comm_tmul`) confirms that the types and instances match. So the definition is exactly the element b ⊗ m.

The definition is a thin wrapper for one sectionwise construction of this library. Mathlib has no declaration of it, only the general `TensorProduct.tmul` and the scoped `ChangeOfRings` notation `b ⊗ₜ[R,f] m`, which is not a declaration. Since the definition only names an element of this specific presheaf construction, the narrow setting is part of what it is, so it is not too narrow. Nothing in it is wrong.
